anomaly_def.Name: MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Excessive accumulation of obsolete row versions, rollback records, and dead index entries outpaces background cleanup, inflating storage and visibility-check costs. 
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly : Write-ahead log generation, flushing, or archival becomes the bottleneck, stalling commits and growing the log store. 
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes saturate host CPU, creating system-wide compute starvation regardless of which layer drives the load. 

When all three conditions coexist, the database exhibits a cascade of symptoms: commit latency and "log write/log flush" waits soar while user transactions also spend more time on MVCC visibility scans and vacuum/garbage-collection contention. Table and index sizes balloon, leading to longer buffer misses and heavier background I/O. Simultaneously, CPU utilization remains pegged; cleanup workers, log-flush daemons, and application sessions compete for cycles, causing elevated run-queue times and mixed wait profiles (CPU, log I/O, MVCC lookup) that are difficult to disentangle. Checkpoints may fire more frequently yet complete more slowly, archiver lag grows, and planner misestimates rise as row-density statistics drift, further inflating CPU and log pressure.

Causally, heavy update/delete churn produces large volumes of undo/redo, first stretching MVCC storage and then flooding the transaction log. The bloated heap forces longer visibility checks, which consume extra CPU; at the same time, intensified log flushing and background vacuum both demand CPU and I/O bandwidth. As CPU saturation lengthens every worker’s service time, cleanup and archiver processes fall further behind, letting dead versions and unarchived logs accumulate. The feedback loop—more dead versions → more log generation → more CPU demand → slower cleanup/flushing—amplifies each anomaly and can tip the database into a write-path stall or emergency shutdown due to version-store or log-space exhaustion.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that waits longer than the specified amount of time while attempting to acquire a lock.
entry.trigger_condition: A statement waits longer than lock_timeout for a table, index, row, or other database object lock.
entry.workload_impact: The statement attempting to acquire the lock is aborted.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
